claim: Only new customer onboarding to Simple AD is not permitted: existing Simple AD customers retain full functionality, their directories and workloads are not affected, and they can continue to create new Simple AD directories.
question: What can existing Simple AD customers still do after the Simple AD availability change?

values.display: Existing Simple AD customers retain full functionality
continue to create new Simple AD directories

evidence.quote: Only new customer onboarding to Simple AD is not permitted. Existing Simple AD customers retain full functionality. Your directories, users, computers, and integrated workloads are not affected, and you can continue to create new Simple AD directories.

claim: Simple AD comes in two sizes: Small supports up to 500 users (about 2,000 objects) and Large supports up to 5,000 users (about 20,000 objects).
question: What sizes does Simple AD come in?

evidence.quote: Small - Supports up to 500 users (approximately 2,000 objects including users, groups, and computers).
Large - Supports up to 5,000 users (approximately 20,000 objects including users, groups, and computers).

claim: An upgrade of AWS Managed Microsoft AD from Standard to Enterprise Edition cannot be reverted, earlier snapshots cannot restore the upgraded directory, the upgrade takes four to five hours, and it adds cost.
question: Can you downgrade AWS Managed Microsoft AD from Enterprise back to Standard Edition after an upgrade?

values.display: it can't be reverted back to its previous edition

evidence.quote: Once your Active Directory is upgraded, it can't be reverted back to its previous edition.
Previous snapshots can't be used to restore the Active Directory after it has been upgraded.
The upgrade process requires four to five hours.
The upgrade will incur additional cost.

note: d029. Upgrade paths today: console, UpdateDirectorySetup API, CLI, PowerShell.

claim: When you add a Region to an AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory, the service creates two domain controllers in the selected VPC in the new Region in the same AWS account, and the directory ID stays the same in all Regions.
question: How many domain controllers does AWS Managed Microsoft AD create in each Region you add with multi-Region replication?

qualifiers.condition: you can add more domain controllers later

evidence.quote: AWS Managed Microsoft AD creates two domain controllers in the selected VPC and deploys them to the new Region in the same AWS account. Your directory identifier (`directory_id`) remains the same across all Regions. You can add additional domain controllers later if you want.

claim: You can extend multi-Region replication of AWS Managed Microsoft AD to additional Regions only if the primary Region is an AWS default Region; with an opt-in primary Region you cannot add Regions.
question: Can an AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory created in an opt-in Region be replicated to more Regions?

values.display: only extend Multi-Region replication to additional Regions

evidence.quote: You can only extend Multi-Region replication to additional Regions if your primary Region is an AWS default Region. If your primary Region is an opt-in Region, you cannot add additional Regions to your Multi-Region replication.

claim: Since 2026-04-01 AWS Managed Microsoft AD supports multi-Region replication in AWS opt-in Regions, except Middle East (UAE) and Middle East (Bahrain); you pay by the hour for the domain controllers in each Region plus cross-Region data transfer.
question: Since when does AWS Managed Microsoft AD multi-Region replication work in opt-in Regions?

values.display: You pay by the hour for the domain controllers
values.spoken: hourly per domain controller, plus data transfer

qualifiers.condition: opt-in Regions except UAE and Bahrain

evidence.quote: Multi-Region replication is available in AWS Opt-In regions where AWS Managed Microsoft AD is available, except the Middle East (UAE) and Middle East (Bahrain) Regions. You pay by the hour for the domain controllers in each region, plus the cross-region data transfer.

evidence.heading: AWS Managed Microsoft AD adds Multi-Region replication for Opt-In regions
